title: Tenali Raman and the Voracious Feast-Goer

full_text:
In Vijayanagara lived a scholar named Bhimasena who had a monstrous, uncontrolled appetite. Whenever a wealthy citizen hosted a wedding or memorial feast, Bhimasena would push his way to the front, eating thirty sweet laddus, ten bowls of ghee payasam, and mountains of rice, until he could barely breathe!
One evening, after devouring an entire banquet at the Prime Minister’s mansion, Bhimasena collapsed upon the courtyard floor, clutching his bloated stomach, groaning in agonizing indigestion:
'Oh, my stomach! I am dying! The food is killing me! Call the physicians!'

The royal physicians prepared heavy doses of bitter castor oil and nauseating herbal pastes, but Bhimasena refused to swallow them, screaming in pain.

Tenali Raman stepped into the room with a smile:
'Step aside, learned doctors! I possess the ancient infallible remedy of Sage Charaka: the Medicine of the Three Miracles!'

Tenali instructed four servants to carry the groaning glutton into a quiet, airy room in his own house.
Tenali placed Bhimasena upon a firm wooden bench.
First Miracle: Tenali brought a large jug of pure warm water with a squeeze of fresh lime juice and a pinch of rock salt:
'Drink this slowly, friend. It will extinguish the fire in thy belly.'
Bhimasena drank, and the warm lime water eased his immediate cramps.

Second Miracle: Tenali bolted the room door from the outside, opened the barred windows to the fresh garden breeze, and announced:
'Now begins the sacred twenty-four-hour Fast of Absolute Silence!
No rice, no laddus, no sweetmeats! Only clean water until tomorrow sunset!'

Bhimasena shrieked and begged for food, but Tenali sat outside on the veranda reading witty stories aloud with his friends, laughing heartily.
Whenever Bhimasena groaned, Tenali shouted through the window:
'Laugh with us, Bhimasena! A hearty laugh shakes the liver, stimulates the digestion, and burns away thirty pounds of greed!'

For twenty-four hours, Bhimasena rested, fasted, drank warm water, and listened to laughter.
By the following evening, his bloated stomach had flattened, his cramps were gone, his fever had cooled, and his tongue was clean and pink!

Tenali unlocked the door and served him a modest, steaming bowl of light moong dal khichdi seasoned with cumin.
Bhimasena ate the simple khichdi, tears of genuine gratitude streaming down his cheeks:
'Tenali! Never in my life has any rich banquet tasted so delicious as this humble bowl of khichdi!'

Tenali smiled warmly:
'Food is medicine when taken with hunger and moderation, but it becomes poison when taken with greed. Remember: the stomach is an engine to serve thy mind, not a bottomless pit to bury thy dignity!'

Bhimasena was cured of his gluttony forever, becoming an advocate of healthy fasting and moderation throughout the city.
moral: Gluttony destroys health and self-respect; moderation and fasting are the truest medicine for body and soul.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Tenali and the Hungry Brahmin"?
options: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
